entries.title: CLI cleanup: postinstall and 2 more
entries.summary: Removed: `cli/release-staging/postinstall.js`, `cli/release/postinstall.js`, `freebuff/cli/release/postinstall.js`.

ai.title: CLI download flow switched to staged download with rollback install
ai.summary: The release CLI now downloads the binary to a partial archive via the new downloadFile routine and separately installs it with a transactional rename (replaceFileWithRollback, commitReplacements, rollbackReplacements), so a failed update rolls back to the previous binary instead of leaving a half-written one. The download also gained proxy env parsing (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY), 303/307/308 redirect support, and resume-aware retry, while the three postinstall.js files were deleted and their npm postinstall/preuninstall scripts removed, moving binary download to first launch. The four index.js copies plus SPEC.md and the three package.json files were updated, affecting cli, cli/release-staging, and freebuff/cli/release.
ai.evidence: In cli/release/staging/index.js and freebuff/cli/release/index.js, the inline download flow was refactored into stageBinary and installStagedBinary with replaceFileWithRollback, rollbackReplacements, commitReplacements, stopRunningProcess, printDownloadFailure, getPartialArchivePath, and checkForUpdates recovery; cli/release-staging/postinstfreebuff/cli/release/postinstall.js and postinstall.js were deleted with their postinstall/preuninstall npm scripts removed from package.json; http.js files gained HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY parsing, protocol-relative proxy handling, 303/307/308 redirect support, and downloadFile.
ai.unknowns: The rollout plan for how existing postinstall-based users transition to first-launch download is not shown in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Split download-and-install into stageBinary and installStagedBinary with transactional rename/rollback and background update recovery in checkForUpdates.
Applied the same staged download, rollback install, and proxy/redirect/retry changes to the staging release launcher.
Mirrored the staged download and rollback install refactor for the Freebuff package, with metadata path and temp dir named for freebuff.
Removed postinstall.js from all three release packages and deleted their postinstall and preuninstall npm scripts, leaving freebuff 0.0.122 and codebuff 1.0.684.

Added HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env parsing, protocol-relative proxy selection, 303/307/308 redirect handling, Range-header resume, and a new downloadFile helper with retryable-content-range logic to http.js.
Updated freebuff/SPEC.md directory structure to list http.js as the release download helper and note first-launch binary download instead of postinstall.js.

facts: Phase 2: Walk backwards through all entries to apply token budgets. Exhausting one role's budget must not evict entries from the other role: user prompts are protected by the user budget independently of how much assistant/tool history the conversation accumulated, and vice versa.

Preserve the pre-existing guarantee that the newest entry always survives, even when it alone exceeds its role's budget. With independent role selection, entries from the other role may still fit, so the old "summary is empty" fallback is no longer sufficient.

entries.summary: Agents changes across 1 file(s) (+105/−25).

ai.title: Context pruner enforces independent role budgets
ai.summary: agents/context-pruner.ts Phase 2 now tracks separate exhaustion flags for user and assistant/tool budgets instead of a single cutoff index. This prevents one role's budget overflow from evicting entries belonging to the other role. The newest entry is explicitly unshifted into the included list if it exceeds its own role's budget, replacing the previous empty-summary fallback.

eli5.text: When a long-running chat hits the token limit, the assistant trims the conversation history to make room, but now it does the trimming in two separate boxes: one for what you typed and one for all the assistant/tool replies. Previously, filling up one box would spill over and start deleting entries from the other; today, exhausting your message budget won't drop the assistant's replies, and overflowing the assistant's budget won't erase your prompts. The most recent message is also explicitly kept even if it alone exceeds its box's limit, replacing the old blank-summary fallback, so the last thing you said or the assistant answered is never silently lost.

facts: Telemetry is best-effort and must never block the actual pruning update.
Ignore logging failures; set_messages below is the critical operation.
Operational events that belong in Axiom but not in product analytics.

CLI logs normally redact structured info payloads before shipping and also mirror a sampled `cli_log` event to PostHog. This allowlist lets a small set of content-free operational events retain useful numeric metadata in Axiom without becoming product events or providing a general redaction bypass.
entries.title: Agents update: context-pruner
entries.summary: New files: `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`.

ai.title: Context pruning emits Axiom-only telemetry bypassing PostHog
ai.summary: The context-pruner agent now reports a context_pruning.completed operational event to the Axiom log sink without mirroring it to PostHog. A new common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts module defines the event name, an allowlist of numeric/string/boolean fields, and a getAxiomOnlyLogEvent sanitizer that drops unknown keys, truncates strings to 200 chars, and discards unexpected types. cli/src/utils/logger.ts calls getAxiomOnlyLogEvent in sendAnalyticsAndLog so allowlisted events skip the cli_log PostHog path and ship their sanitized data to /api/logs, while common/src/schemas/logs.ts and common/src/types/contracts/logs.ts broaden the event field comments from AnalyticsEvent to Analytics or operational event name. Pruning telemetry is wrapped in a try/catch so a logging failure never blocks the set_messages call, and the pruner now tracks per-role budgets and live-user-prompt preservation metadata.
ai.evidence: New file common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts defines CONTEXT_PRUNING_COMPLETED_EVENT, an allowlist CONTEXT_PRUNING_FIELDS, and getAxiomOnlyLogEvent, which is imported and invoked in cli/src/utils/logger.ts sendAnalyticsAndLog to bypass PostHog and ship sanitized numeric metadata to the Axiom /api/logs sink; agents/context-pruner.ts now receives logger in handleSteps and emits a best-effort logger.info with axiomEvent: CONTEXT_PRUNING_COMPLETED_EVENT after computing pruning metrics, guarded so logging failures do not block set_messages
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which consumer reads the context_pruning.completed event from Axiom or whether the telemetry rollout is gated per environment.

changes.what: New allowlist-based sanitizer that recognizes the context_pruning.completed event and retains only its declared numeric, string, and boolean fields.
Imports and calls getAxiomOnlyLogEvent to route allowlisted events to Axiom only, bypassing PostHog and using the sanitized data for the /api/logs record.
Accepts logger in handleSteps and emits a best-effort context_pruning.completed event with pruning metrics, guarded so logging failures do not block set_messages.

ai.title: Read files tool enforces shared character and token limits
ai.summary: The read files tool now enforces a 100,000-character hard limit and a 20,000 estimated-token limit that are shared across all files in a single call, via a new createFileReadLimiter imported into the SDK's getFiles routine. Previously each file was truncated independently against a fixed 100,000-character threshold with no combined token budget. Affected files: common/src/util/file-read-limits.ts (new), sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts, agents/types/tools.ts, and common/src/tools/params/tool/read-files.ts.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/util/file-read-limits.ts` exports `createFileReadLimiter` with `MAX_READ_FILES_CHARS = 100_000` and `MAX_READ_FILES_TOKENS = 20_000`; `sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts` imports it and replaces the old `MAX_CHARS` slicing with `limiter.limit(content)`, and the `read_files` schema description in `agents/types/tools.ts` and `common/src/tools/params/tool/read-files.ts` now states the shared 20,000 token / 100,000 character limits.

changes.what: Added new file-read-limits module exporting the shared limiter factory and the MAX_READ_FILES_CHARS and MAX_READ_FILES_TOKENS constants.
Replaced inline MAX_CHARS truncation in getFiles with the new createFileReadLimiter that enforces both character and token budgets across all requested files.
Updated the read_files tool description in the shared type definitions to document the shared 20,000 token and 100,000 character limits.
Updated the read_files input schema description to state the shared estimated-token and character limits, guiding users to prefer smaller file sets and use code_search.
